note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for prostate cancer management following recent PSA rise and persistent high-risk histological features.

Recently retired civil engineer with a history of hypertension and benign prostatic hyperplasia. Current medications include valsartan, lisinopril, metoprolol, and tamsulosin. Reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 13/35. Non-smoker, consumes 20 units of alcohol weekly, and walks 45 minutes daily. Married, lives with partner, adult son serves as primary contact. Recent ophthalmology review for cataracts and biannual dental check-up completed. No new bone pain or haematuria reported.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged without nodularity or induration, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs and no palpable lymphadenopathy.
